chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Bukayr from Ubaydullah al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about forgetfulness (sahw), for it occurs frequently with me, so he said, 'Integrate your prayer with integration.' I said, 'And what is the integration?' He said, 'Three glorifications (tasbihat) in the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud).'

key_terms.إِدْرَاج: Integration or smooth incorporation (a technical term for a specific compensation method)

ai.seo_question: How to correct frequent forgetfulness during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the common issue of *sahw* (forgetfulness) by prescribing a preventive measure rather than a post-prayer correction. He instructs the worshipper to recite three glorifications (*tasbihat*) during both *ruku'* and *sujud*, a practice that stabilizes the prayer structure and minimizes doubt. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on practical ease (*taysir*) and the importance of maintaining concentration (*khushu*) through consistent devotional acts during the physical postures of prayer.
